topic: The LIV Method to Expand NYC Footprint, Open Largest Studio Yet

facts.label: Story
facts.value: The LIV Method to Expand NYC Footprint, Open Largest Studio Yet

facts.label: Article
facts.value: The boutique fitness operator, which offers private, semi-private and group training, will soon open its third location in New York City New York City-based boutique fitness brand the LIV Method is expanding its Manhattan footprint with the opening of a third location. Set to open in January 2027, the new space, located at 2 Gansevoort in the Meatpacking/West Village area, will be the brand’s largest to date, at 12,000 square feet. Members there will experience the LIV Method’s signature private, semi-private and group training sessions, with access to recovery amenities including cold plunges, a sauna and practitioner treatments. The brand’s methodology focuses on personalized injury prevention and performance optimization through individual assessment of each client’s strengths and weaknesses, with strength, cardio and dynamic mobility movements. credit: The LIV Method The deal, brokered by real estate advisory firm Dennis Healthcare, situates the family-owned, family-operated and self-funded business in a designated NYC landmark, part of the Greenwich Village Historic District. “2 Gansevoort is the next neighborhood we call home. We don’t just enter a neighborhood; we become part of its fabric,” founder Matt Sauerhoff and chief operating officer Danielle Krinsky told Athletech News in a joint statement.

topic: Jazzercise Founder Judi Sheppard Missett to Be Inducted into the 2027 HFA Hall of Fame

facts.label: Story
facts.value: Jazzercise Founder Judi Sheppard Missett to Be Inducted into the 2027 HFA Hall of Fame

facts.label: Article
facts.value: The aerobic exercise trailblazer transformed fitness programming with her dance-based exercise classes and continues to influence fitness and women’s entrepreneurship today. Washington, DC–October 19, 2026– For more than five decades, Judi Sheppard Missett has helped shape the modern fitness industry, transforming a class of 15 women into a global movement that brought dance fitness into the mainstream, created new paths to entrepreneurship, and helped millions of people experience the benefits of physical activity. Jazzercise has proven it’s more than a fitness fad, evolving into an industry leader through constant innovation. On March 10, 2027, the Health & Fitness Association (HFA) will recognize Missett’s contributions and continuing influence by inducting the Jazzercise founder and executive chair into the Health & Fitness Hall of Fame during the opening night of The HFA Show 2027 in Las Vegas. “Judi is a true pioneer,” said HFA Interim President and CEO Greta Wagner. “She changed the way millions of people experience fitness and created opportunities for generations of women to become entrepreneurs. More than five decades later, she continues to influence our industry as Jazzercise evolves and reaches new generations.” Missett’s idea for Jazzercise began while she was teaching at the Chicago-area studio of jazz dance legend Gus Giordano.
